speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific nature of your dizziness and vertigo, and how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or a decrease in hearing during these dizzy spells, and do these episodes occur when you change your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). I am requesting images of your Dix-Hallpike maneuver results to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Dix-Hallpike_Manuever_Results
